name: n8n
description: n8n is a workflow automation tool with hosted cloud plans and a self-hosted Community Edition on GitHub.
features: EU hosting in Frankfurt for hosted plans
strengths: Hosted data is stored in the EU
limitations: The Business plan is self-hosted only (hosted availability is waitlisted)
Business and Enterprise self-hosted instances require a licence key checked daily
No USD list prices on the page

plans.name: Business
plans.note: Billed annually; 40k workflow executions; the page says Business is self-hosted only. Earlier check showed EUR 667.

pricing.trial: n8n Cloud trial with no credit card: 1,000 executions, 5 concurrent executions, 180-second timeout. Business trial: 14 days, card required.
pricing.regional: The page showed USD ($) on this visit; an earlier visit showed euros, so the displayed currency may depend on the visitor. Hosted plans store data in Frankfurt, Germany.
notes: Monthly-billed prices are not stated. A free plan is not stated, but the self-hosted Community Edition is available on GitHub (licence terms not stated on the page).

openSource.note: The repository describes n8n as fair-code under the Sustainable Use License; it does not call it open source

profile.headline: Build AI agents and workflows you can follow step by step

capabilities.title: Build visually, then drop into code
capabilities.text: A visual builder for workflows, with the option to write code whenever you need it.

capabilities.title: Connect your tools
capabilities.text: More than 500 native integrations, any API through HTTP, and any agent or coding assistant through MCP.

capabilities.title: Watch agents work
capabilities.text: See agents run live or open any past run to check what happened.

capabilities.title: Put rules around AI actions
capabilities.text: Use structured inputs and outputs, human-in-the-loop approvals and rule-based automation.

featureCards.name: Recover in one step
featureCards.text: Spot an error and re-run just the step that broke.

featureCards.name: Every change tracked
featureCards.text: Version history shows who changed what and when.

featureCards.name: Replay and mock data
featureCards.text: Replay a past run or mock the data, and read exactly what happened in the logs.

featureCards.name: Built-in documentation
featureCards.text: The workflow itself serves as its documentation.

featureCards.name: Self-hosting
featureCards.text: Deploy on your own servers or with Docker, or use the hosted version; the source code is on GitHub.

featureCards.name: Enterprise controls
featureCards.text: SAML SSO, LDAP, encrypted secret stores, role-based access, audit logs, log streaming and AI governance with guardrails and evaluations.

audienceDetail.text: The site speaks to small teams as well as enterprises, and cites Fortune 500 customers.
A community of more than 250,000 developers, and a builder that lets you drop into code.
Alert triage and threat investigation are among the example workflows.
Lead qualification is one of the listed use cases.

scenarios.title: Handle a refund
scenarios.text: Look up an order, then ask for approval on Slack before refunding or opening a ticket.

scenarios.title: Onboard a new user
scenarios.text: Run onboarding steps across Slack, Jira and Notion.

scenarios.title: Investigate a threat
scenarios.text: Check suspicious indicators against several security tools and summarise the findings with AI.

scenarios.title: Qualify leads
scenarios.text: An AI agent answers messages, qualifies the lead, updates the record and sends a reply.

gettingStarted.text: Use the Get Started link for the hosted version, or deploy it yourself with Docker.
Use the visual builder, and add code only where you need it.
The site lists templates such as Process invoice, Knowledge assistant and Daily News Digest.
Talk to sales about enterprise options.
